action: Customers of JPMorgan and Mastercard benefit programs: expect phishing that uses your name or email, and do not act on unsolicited messages.
date_note: Date of the companies' statements: ABC13 (read 2026-11-19) says JPMorganChase made its statement Thursday morning (19 November); the date of the attack itself is not stated.
exec: Vendor breach exposed marketing data at major payment and banking brands; phishing risk for customers.
plain: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say outside vendors were hacked. JPMorgan and Mastercard say some customer email addresses may be exposed; they say card payment data was not.
summary: JPMorganChase said third-party providers were hit by a cyberattack and it believes attackers accessed marketing data that may include some customer names and email addresses; it reported no service disruption. Mastercard cited limited cardholder email addresses; Visa said its systems and payments data were not affected. The n0n gang's involvement is a claim reported by Yahoo Finance citing SOCRadar.
title: Visa says incident was at an Asia Pacific third-party provider after n0n gang lists it and JPMorgan
